subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes permission-sensitive fallback semantics across session, auth/provider, and channel routing boundaries, and repository policy treats fallback behavior as a product/security decision.

options.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Bindings Only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and add doctor/status guidance for Discord accounts that appear intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair Fork PR First
options.body: Use the open fork PR as source material only after resolving conflicts, adding a configured-agent guard and distinct matchedBy value, and supplying real Discord proof.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on multi-agent routing and the shared resolver where the contract decision lands.
